summary: TRILL has a campus-wide MTU feature so link-state updates can always be flooded while still allowing jumbo packets. This document adds a way to negotiate MTU on links, so a TRILL campus can work out the packet size it can safely use.

eli5.summary: Everyone agrees on the biggest box that fits through every door in the building, so no box gets stuck.

questions: how does trill test link mtu
what is the difference between sz and lz in trill
subtitle: Lets TRILL neighbors use the larger packet sizes their shared link can really carry, and tests link MTU with a binary search.

tldr.problem: TRILL RBridges format link-state PDUs to fit a campus-wide minimum size called Sz, so link-local PDUs cannot use a larger MTU even when the link supports it. The old MTU test was also not efficient.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 8249 adds a link-wide size Lz, advertised in a new originatingSNPBufferSize APPsub-TLV, lets link-local PDUs be as big as the tested link MTU, and defines a binary search algorithm for testing link MTU with few probes.
tldr.outcome: Link-local PDUs such as CSNPs and PSNPs can be larger than Sz, which can reduce the number of PDUs and speed up link-state synchronization. RFC 8249 updates RFC 6325, RFC 7177 and RFC 7780.

today: RFC 8249 is a Proposed Standard from September 2017 that updates RFC 6325, RFC 7177 and RFC 7780, and the unit metadata shows no later RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why TRILL Needs Two Sizes
sections.content:
RFC 6325 describes how RBridges agree on a campus-wide minimum acceptable inter-RBridge MTU, called Sz, so that link-state flooding works and all RBridges converge to the same link state. All RBridges format their Link State PDUs (LSPs) to fit in Sz. RFC 7177 includes the event "Link MTU size is successfully tested" in the transition of an adjacency from the 2-Way state to the Report state. A link that cannot support Sz is not reported as part of the campus topology.

RFC 8249 specifies a new RECOMMENDED link-wide minimum MTU size, Lz. With it, link-scoped PDUs can be formatted larger than Sz, up to the link-wide limit, which can make link use more efficient and speed up link-state convergence.

It also specifies an optional, more efficient MTU testing algorithm that is backward compatible with the old method, and it updates RFC 6325, RFC 7177 and RFC 7780.
sections.eli5: The whole building uses small boxes so they fit every door. Two neighbors with a wider door between them can use bigger boxes, which means fewer trips.

sections.title: Link-Wide Lz and Campus-Wide Sz
sections.content:
Link-wide Lz is the minimum Lz supported and agreed upon by all RBridges on one link. If the link is usable, Lz is greater than or equal to Sz. Some TRILL IS-IS PDUs are exchanged only between neighbors, such as Complete Sequence Number PDUs (CSNPs) and Partial Sequence Number PDUs (PSNPs). They are confined by Lz instead of Sz. TRILL IS-IS Hellos are link local too, but are always limited to 1470 bytes for robustness.

RBridges exchange their maximum supported Lz using Extended L1 Circuit Scope (E-L1CS) flooding scope LSPs. The smallest advertised value on a link, but not less than Sz, is the link-wide Lz. E-L1CS FS-LSPs can also be sent up to Lz, but fragment zero MUST NOT exceed 1470 bytes.

Sz keeps working as before. RBridges still propagate originatingL1LSPBufferSize through LSPs, the smallest advertised value (not below 1470) is deemed Sz, and campus-wide PDUs such as LSPs are formatted no greater than Sz.

Agreement on Lz does not prove that PDUs of that size get through. The RFC's example has three RBridges with Lz 1800 and an intermediate bridge whose port MTU is 1700, which would discard 1800-byte PDUs. For that reason the link MTU SHOULD be tested.
sections.eli5: Sz is the box size that fits every door in the whole building. Lz is the biggest box that fits every door on one hallway. A hidden narrow door in the hallway is why they still test it.

sections.title: The originatingSNPBufferSize APPsub-TLV
sections.content:
An RBridge advertises its value in an originatingSNPBufferSize APPsub-TLV, which SHOULD be included in a TRILL GENINFO TLV in fragment zero of its E-L1CS FS-LSP. Its value comes from the management parameter originatingL1SNPBufferSize. Only fragment zero counts, and if several of these sub-TLVs appear there, the one with the smallest value, but not below 1470 bytes, is used.

If the sub-TLV is missing, the originating system is assumed to be advertising Sz octets. The type is 21 and the length is 2. The value is an unsigned integer limited to the range 1470 to 65,535 bytes, and a value below 1470 is ignored. IANA has assigned type 21 in the TRILL APPsub-TLV Types registry.
sections.eli5: Each neighbor writes down the biggest box it can handle on a small card and shares it. The card has a fixed layout so everyone reads it the same way.

sections.title: Binary Search for Link MTU
sections.content:
RB1 searches for the link MTU by sending MTU-probe PDUs and waiting for MTU-ack replies from RB2. It starts with a probe padded to link-wide Lz. If an ack arrives within k tries (default 3), the link MTU is Lz and the search stops.

Otherwise RB1 probes at 1470 bytes. If that fails after k tries, RB1 sets the "failed minimum MTU test" flag for RB2 in its Hello. If it succeeds, the link MTU is 1470, lowerBound is 1470 and upperBound is Lz. RB1 then probes the midpoint x, rounded down. A failure sets upperBound to x - 1. An ack sets the link MTU and lowerBound to x. The search stops when the bounds meet or after n repeats (default 5).

It is RECOMMENDED that one round-trip time separate successive probes, with 5 milliseconds assumed if the operator cannot estimate it. Testing is done only in the Designated VLAN, and the Designated RBridge (DRB) is RECOMMENDED to do it. Multicast probes are used when several RBridges should answer.

Afterwards, whether the link supports Sz can often be decided without more probes: if lowerBound is at least Sz it does, and if upperBound is at most Sz it does not. If Sz lies strictly between the bounds, RBridges SHOULD probe at Sz; if they do not, the only safe assumption is that the link cannot support Sz.
sections.eli5: It is like guessing a number by always picking the middle. Try a box size; if it fits, guess bigger, if not, guess smaller. A few guesses find the biggest box that fits.

sections.title: Refreshing Sz and Synchronizing LSPs
sections.content:
When an RBridge joins with an originatingL1LSPBufferSize smaller than the current Sz, other RBridges lower Sz, and any LSP larger than the new Sz MUST be split or redistributed. A joining RBridge with an equal or greater value changes nothing. When an RBridge whose value equals Sz leaves, its LSPs are purged after MaxAge and Sz MAY be recalculated and MAY increase. Its value counts even for IS-IS unreachable RBridges, which updates RFC 7780.

Frequent LSP resizing is harmful, so upward resizing SHOULD be dampened. A timer LSPresizeTime, default 300 seconds, is RECOMMENDED, and upward resizing before it expires is ignored.

For synchronization, CSNPs and PSNPs may be formatted up to link-wide Lz but are processed normally if larger. Before the link MTU has been tested, a larger PDU may be discarded, but once tested, RBridges format PDUs within that MTU. A port whose MTU is smaller than the local originatingL1SNPBufferSize SHOULD be disabled. An LSP too large for a port MUST NOT be sent on it, and an LSPTooLargeToPropagate alarm is generated.
sections.eli5: If a new neighbor can only handle small boxes, everyone shrinks their boxes. When they leave, people wait a while before going back to big boxes so they do not keep changing their minds.

sections.title: Backward Compatibility and Traffic MTU
sections.content:
Links can mix Lz-aware and Lz-ignorant RBridges. This behaves properly, though less efficiently than if all were Lz aware. Lz-ignorant RBridges always format PDUs no larger than Sz, which Lz-aware receivers can handle. Lz-aware senders may send larger link-local PDUs, which Lz-ignorant receivers can handle because their buffer size was already tested. An RBridge following RFC 6325 that receives an MTU-probe MUST reply with an MTU-ack padded to the same size.

Sz and Lz limit most TRILL IS-IS PDUs, not TRILL Data packets, which are limited by the physical MTU of the ports they cross. The same algorithm can test traffic MTU, with the sending port's MTU replacing Lz, and the result MAY be advertised in the MTU sub-TLV of RFC 7176. End stations do not take part in TRILL IS-IS, so an operator may use tools such as TRILL ping or traceroute to find the path MTU.
sections.eli5: Neighbors who do not know the new trick still work fine with those who do. They just do not get the speed-up.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC raises no significant new security issues. RBridges are generally considered trusted devices, and forged PDUs, including forged Hellos carrying the new sub-TLV, can be addressed with IS-IS cryptographic authentication from RFC 5310. The worst an RBridge can do by reporting an erroneous originatingSNPBufferSize is reduce Lz to Sz, which removes the optimization of using link MTUs above the campus-wide MTU for link-local PDUs.
sections.eli5: Even if someone lies about their box size, the worst result is that everyone uses the smaller, safe size again.

fields.desc: TRILL APPsub-TLV type 21; two bytes because it appears in an extended TLV.
